title: The Quiet Minute
credit: Built on Robert's preview rewrite (preview-stories-e4e6722) and the 7 November played script. Rewritten on 8 November so that listening is the control: who you turn to gets the floor.
premise: You chair tonight. The room is booked until ten, and the route for two hundred new students has to be agreed before then.
lesson: Your attention gave the floor. The format decided who kept it.

Nia.aria: Nia, in the teal cardigan, with a folded map she walked today

Theo.aria: Theo, in the rust shirt, his hand on the model he built

Ellis.aria: Ellis, in the plum shirt and glasses, a folded sheet under his hand

qm2-01.speaker: Theo
qm2-01.line: Main gate, the courtyard, then down to the harbour just as the lights come on. That's the moment. That's what they'll remember.

L-t2.speaker: Theo
L-t2.line: Two hundred students, one photo at the water. I've timed it twice. Forty minutes, door to harbour.
L-t2.direction: enthusiastic, counting it off, confident in the details

L-t3.speaker: Theo
L-t3.line: My first night here, nobody walked me anywhere. I found the harbour on my own, near midnight, a bit lost. I want them to find it together.
L-t3.direction: quieter and more personal, the bravado drops for a moment; sincere, a little embarrassed

L-t4.speaker: Theo
L-t4.line: The model's done. We just need to agree it tonight.
L-t4.direction: brisk, upbeat, wrapping up, hand patting the model

L-t5.speaker: Theo
L-t5.line: Twelve minutes. So, are we agreed?
L-t5.direction: glancing at the clock, hopeful, assuming the answer is yes

qm2-03.speaker: Theo
qm2-03.line: Is a great photo stop, I know. Ten minutes there, tops.

qm2-05.speaker: Theo
qm2-05.line: Security will open it if we ask. It'll be fine.

qm2-04.speaker: Nia
qm2-04.line: No, I mean it's locked. After six. I checked today.

qm2-r2.speaker: Nia
qm2-r2.line: The courtyard gate locks at six. If we start there at half five, it's still open, and we're not stuck outside with two hundred people.

L-n2.speaker: Nia
L-n2.line: So we start there at half five, while it's still open. Courtyard first.
L-n2.direction: steadier now that someone is listening, practical and clear

L-n3.speaker: Nia
L-n3.line: And it's not only the gate. The courtyard's where I met my first friend here. I want them to see it.
L-n3.direction: softer, a little exposed, it matters to her personally; honest

L-n0.speaker: Nia
L-n0.direction: quietly giving up, deflated, under her breath

L-e1.speaker: Ellis
L-e1.line: I... drew another one. A different route.
L-e1.direction: hesitant, shy, surprised to be asked, almost apologetic

L-e2.speaker: Ellis
L-e2.line: It starts at the courtyard. Early, while it's still light.
L-e2.direction: gaining a little confidence, explaining carefully

L-e3.speaker: Ellis
L-e3.line: Then up the hill to the open ground. You can see the whole campus from there. It never reaches the harbour, though.
L-e3.direction: warmer, picturing it, then a careful apology at the end

L-e0.speaker: Ellis
L-e0.direction: trailing off, retreating, quiet and small

qm2-r1.speaker: You
qm2-r1.line: Let's go round once. One concern each, and nobody replies until everyone's spoken. Nia, you first.

qm2-r4.speaker: Ellis
qm2-r4.line: That's where mine starts, actually. The courtyard. But it never reaches the harbour. I know that's the part you love, Theo.

qm2-r5.speaker: Theo
qm2-r5.line: It is. Show me your first stop.

L-ry1.speaker: You
L-ry1.line: Theo, I heard why the harbour matters. Could it be its own night, later in the week?

L-ry2.speaker: Theo
L-ry2.line: Its own night. Okay. Show me your first stop, Ellis.
L-ry2.direction: disappointed but touched that someone remembered; turning to Ellis with real interest

L-rk1.speaker: Nia
L-rk1.line: That's the room. We still haven't got an ending.

L-rk2.speaker: Theo
L-rk2.direction: a small, generous concession, a little sad

qm2-s1.speaker: You
qm2-s1.line: Everyone, write down one thing that worries you about tomorrow. No names. Then we'll read them together.

L-s2.speaker: You
L-s2.line: Gate locked after six. Too crowded at the harbour. A different start?
L-s2.direction: reading three slips aloud, one by one, thoughtful, small pauses between them

qm2-s3.speaker: You
qm2-s3.line: So the courtyard's the problem. We drop it?

qm2-s4.speaker: Nia
qm2-s4.line: No, don't drop it. The courtyard's where I met my first friend here. I want them to see it. Just go there first.

qm2-s5.speaker: You
qm2-s5.line: Sorry. I read that too fast. Courtyard first.

L-s3h.speaker: You
L-s3h.line: So the gate's the problem, not the courtyard. Courtyard first, before six?
L-s3h.direction: careful, reading it right, checking with Nia

L-s6h.speaker: Ellis
L-s6h.line: The different start is mine. Here.
L-s6h.direction: quiet but brave, sliding a folded sheet across the table

L-s7h.speaker: Theo
L-s7h.line: Courtyard at half five. That works with the gate.
L-s7h.direction: reading the sheet, surprised and grudgingly impressed

L-sk1.speaker: Theo
L-sk1.line: Too crowded at the harbour. Who wrote that?
L-sk1.direction: stung, trying to sound casual and failing

qm2-07.speaker: You
qm2-07.line: Twenty minutes left, and I've only really heard one person.

facts.theo.plan: Theo's route ends at the harbour as the lights come on.
facts.theo.why: Theo found the harbour alone, lost, on his first night. He wants the new students to find it together.
facts.nia.gate: The courtyard gate locks at six. Nia checked today.
facts.nia.plan: Start at half five, while the gate is open: courtyard first.
facts.nia.why: The courtyard is where Nia met her first friend here.
facts.ellis.route: Ellis has drawn a different route.
facts.ellis.start: It starts at the courtyard, early, while it is light.
facts.ellis.end: It ends on the open ground, with the whole campus in view. No harbour.

round.label: Turn the table
round.hint: Everyone heard, in turn. It takes the time it takes.
round.aria: Turn the table: everyone speaks once, in turn, before anyone replies. Everyone is heard, but it takes the time it takes.

slips.label: Pass the slips
slips.hint: Quick, and nobody has to speak up. No names, though.
slips.aria: Pass the slips: everyone writes one worry, no names, then you read them together. Quick, and nobody has to speak up, but you won't know who wrote what.

round.text: You asked me. Nobody usually does. The sheet's yours now, with the gate drawn on it.
You knew why the harbour mattered, and it still went. Its own night, you said. I'm holding you to that.
The harbour was the part they'd have remembered. I'll get over it. Not tonight.
We started with me, for once. We still haven't got an ending. Seven o'clock, before class?

slips.text: You read my slip the way I meant it. I didn't have to explain twice.
You read my slip too fast. Thank you for stopping when I said so.
I only owned up to the slip because you'd already listened once. Full route attached.
I wrote 'a different start?'. I don't think you knew it was me. The sheet's still in my bag.
